subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A potential benefit of using stem cells in medicine is that they could be used to:
options: Grow replacement cells or tissues, such as nerve cells for paralysis
Increase the number of chromosomes in cells
questions.explain: Stem cells could be made to differentiate into needed cell types, for example to replace damaged tissues.

questions.q: Why might stem cells from a patient's own body be preferred for treating a condition?
options: They are less likely to be rejected by the patient's immune system
They are easier to grow than other cells
They contain twice the normal number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Cells taken from the patient's own body have the same genes, so they are less likely to be rejected.

questions.q: Which chambers of the heart receive blood returning to the heart?
questions.explain: The atria are the upper chambers that receive blood entering the heart.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a stem cell and a specialised cell such as a nerve cell?
options: A stem cell is unspecialised and can divide to form different cell types
A specialised cell can become any other type of cell
A stem cell has more chromosomes
questions.explain: Stem cells are unspecialised and can differentiate into many cell types, unlike specialised cells.

questions.q: What is differentiation?
options: A cell dividing into two identical cells
A cell becoming specialised for a particular function
questions.explain: Differentiation is the process by which cells become specialised for a specific job.

questions.q: How many cells are produced from one parent cell by mitosis?
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical cells (meiosis, not mitosis, makes four).

questions.q: Which change would slow down the rate of diffusion of a substance into a cell?
options: Increasing the surface area of the membrane
questions.explain: A greater diffusion distance (a thicker barrier) reduces the rate of diffusion.

questions.q: Animal cells placed in pure water can burst, but plant cells in pure water do not. This is because plant cells have a:
questions.explain: The cell wall is strong and resists the pressure as water enters, stopping the plant cell bursting.

questions.q: Why are xylem vessels strengthened with lignin?
options: To keep them hollow and support the plant
questions.explain: Lignin strengthens xylem vessels, keeping them open and helping support the plant.

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is used to estimate the rate of water uptake by a shoot?
questions.explain: A potometer measures water uptake, used to investigate transpiration rate.

questions.q: Translocation in the phloem requires energy because it is...
options: an active process moving dissolved food to where it is needed
questions.explain: Translocation is an active process that moves dissolved sugars around the plant.

questions.q: Which of these is an ethical concern raised against the use of embryonic stem cells?
options: Embryos that could develop into a person are destroyed
They are too easy to grow
questions.explain: A key objection is that obtaining embryonic stem cells involves destroying embryos.

questions.q: As an organism gets larger, its surface area to volume ratio:
questions.explain: Larger organisms have a smaller surface area to volume ratio, so they need specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of transpiration?
questions.explain: Moving air carries away water vapour, keeping a steep gradient and increasing transpiration.

questions.q: What is the 'transpiration stream'?
options: The movement of air through stomata
Water draining out of the soil
The flow of sugars in phloem
The continuous movement of water from roots up through the xylem to the leaves
questions.explain: As water evaporates from leaves, more is pulled up through the xylem in the transpiration stream.

questions.q: In a capillary, substances such as glucose and oxygen leave the blood by which process?
options: Diffusion across the thin capillary wall
questions.explain: Substances diffuse between blood and tissues across the one-cell-thick capillary walls.

questions.q: In an osmosis experiment, why should the potato chips be dried with a paper towel before being reweighed?
options: To remove surface liquid so only the change inside the chip is measured
To kill the cells before weighing
questions.explain: Drying removes excess surface solution so the recorded mass reflects water moving in or out of the cells, not liquid clinging to the surface.

questions.q: What is the function of valves in the heart and veins?
questions.explain: Valves ensure blood flows in one direction only and prevent backflow.

questions.q: Osmosis is the movement of:
options: Water from a concentrated to a dilute solution
Any dissolved solute across a membrane
Water from a dilute to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
Particles from high to low concentration using ATP
questions.explain: Osmosis is the diffusion of water only, from a dilute (high water) to a more concentrated (low water) solution through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: What is the main role of platelets?
questions.explain: Platelets are cell fragments that help the blood clot at wounds.

questions.q: Which statement about xylem is correct?
options: It is made of living cells and carries sugars
It transports food in both directions
It is made of dead cells strengthened with lignin and carries water
questions.explain: Xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes strengthened by lignin that carry water upwards.

questions.q: Water moves into a cell by osmosis when the cell is surrounded by a solution with:
options: A higher water concentration than the cell
The same water concentration as the cell
A lower water concentration than the cell
questions.explain: Water moves from where there is more water (more dilute solution) into the cell.
